title: NoSQL vs SQL

sections.content: NoSQL databases (MongoDB, Redis, Cassandra) trade relational guarantees for flexibility: document/key-value/wide-column stores scale horizontally and handle unstructured data.
Choose SQL when data is structured with relationships and ACID matters; choose NoSQL for flexible schemas, massive scale, or simple key lookups. Many systems use both (polyglot persistence).
Key points: "NoSQL" means "not only SQL" not "no SQL", joins are rare in NoSQL (denormalize instead), and transactions exist but with caveats.
